# Results — Study 322 (FOMC-Blackout) on the real SPY tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Each SPY trading day since
1994 is flagged as inside / outside the ~10-day pre-meeting FOMC communications blackout
(the trading days within 10 calendar days before a scheduled decision), and we measure
the blackout-vs-rest mean, HAC and Welch t-stats, a calendar-shift placebo, a pre/post-
2011 split, the volatility ("calm?") check, and a cost-swept long-only-in-blackout timing
book. Data: SPY daily auto-adjusted (total-return proxy). As-of **2026-06-12** (the last
complete bar in the pinned cache); match the fingerprint to confirm you hold the same
tape.*

## Data stamp

| Tape | Window | Days | Fingerprint |
|---|---|--:|---|
| SPY total-return | 1994-01-03 → 2026-06-12 | 8,166 | `c35148b53fca` |

Blackout days: **1,741** · non-blackout days: **6,425** (≈21% of the sample).

## The headline — blackout vs the rest of the year (daily total return)

| Arm | n | mean (bps/day) | HAC *t* | ann. Sharpe |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Blackout (~10 days pre-meeting) | 1,741 | **+5.00** | **+2.02** | +0.66 |
| Non-blackout | 6,425 | +4.73 | +3.72 | +0.64 |
| All days | 8,166 | +4.79 | +4.26 | +0.64 |
| **Difference (blackout − other)** | | **+0.27** | **Welch *t* = +0.08** | |

- The blackout window earns **+5.00 bps/day** — but so does every other day (+4.73 bps).
  The blackout level clears the bar on its own (HAC *t* = +2.02) only because it is **being
  long a rising index**, not because of anything special about the quiet period.
- The decisive number is the **difference**: **+0.27 bps/day, Welch *t* = +0.08.** That is
  indistinguishable from zero. There is **no excess "blackout drift."**

## Calm before the storm? — volatility inside vs outside the window

| Arm | annualised vol (bps) |
|---|--:|
| Blackout | 1,922 |
| Non-blackout | 1,866 |
| **Ratio** | **1.030** |

The blackout window is **not** calmer — its volatility is marginally *higher* (ratio
1.03). The "calm before the storm" framing is busted on the data: the run-up is just an
ordinary stretch of market, not a lull.

## Calendar-shift placebo — slide the window and re-measure the diff

| Window offset (cal. days) | diff (bps) | Welch *t* |
|--:|--:|--:|
| −20 | +3.67 | +1.11 |
| −10 | +0.01 | +0.00 |
| −5 | −0.09 | −0.03 |
| **0 (true rule)** | **+0.27** | **+0.08** |
| +5 | −0.33 | −0.11 |
| +10 | +0.34 | +0.11 |
| +20 | +1.58 | +0.51 |

The diff at the true window (offset 0) is *smaller* than at several arbitrary shifts. A
real effect would peak at offset 0; this profile is flat noise. The "blackout" label
carries no special information.

## Pre/post-2011 — any drift, and did it decay?

| Era | diff (bps) | Welch *t* | n blackout |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Pre-2011 | +2.67 | +0.57 | 890 |
| Post-2011 (after Lucca-Moench) | **−2.35** | **−0.53** | 851 |

Even the sign flips: a small, insignificant *positive* diff pre-2011 becomes a small,
insignificant *negative* diff afterwards. Neither era clears |*t*| = 2.

## Could you trade it? — the long-only-in-blackout timing book

Hold SPY only on blackout days, cash otherwise. ~16 one-way trips/yr (two per meeting):

| round-trip cost | book gross %/yr | book net %/yr | buy-and-hold %/yr |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.0 bps (gross) | +2.69 | +2.69 | +12.07 |
| 1.0 bps | +2.69 | +2.53 | +12.07 |
| 2.0 bps | +2.69 | +2.36 | +12.07 |
| 5.0 bps | +2.69 | +1.87 | +12.07 |

- The timing book earns **+2.69%/yr gross** vs buy-and-hold's **+12.07%/yr** — it captures
  only the slice of drift that happens to fall in the window (it is in the market ~21% of
  the time), and gives up the other ~79% of the year's return.
- Excess-of-cash Sharpe: **book +0.30** vs **buy-and-hold +0.64.** The book is strictly
  worse on a risk-adjusted basis even *before* costs. This is a mirage on the Tradability
  axis: there is no edge to harvest, only a fraction of beta.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is a faithful detector

On the deterministic synthetic tape the same machinery recovers a planted effect only
when one is present (and scores ~0 on the null):

| Planted | blackout HAC *t* | diff (bps) | Welch *t* | vol ratio |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Null (excess 0, vol ×1) | — | −0.16 | −0.04 | ≈1.0 |
| +15 bps/day blackout excess | +5.08 | +14.84 | +3.44 | ≈1.0 |
| Calm (vol ×0.5, no excess) | — | ≈0 | ≈0 | 0.48 |

The harness banks a planted excess (Welch *t* = +3.44) and a planted "calm" (vol ratio
0.48) — so its *failure* to find either on the real tape is evidence about the market, not
a dead pipeline.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Blackout-minus-other diff **+0.27 bps/day, Welch *t* = +0.08**; the
  placebo profile is flat (offset 0 is not a peak); the pre/post-2011 sign even flips. The
  blackout window earns ordinary equity drift and nothing more.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** A long-only-in-blackout book earns +2.69%/yr vs +12.07%/yr
  buy-and-hold, with a *lower* excess Sharpe (0.30 vs 0.64) even before costs — it is a
  fraction of beta, not an edge.
- **Calm before the storm? — BUSTED.** Blackout-window volatility is marginally *higher*
  (ratio 1.03), not lower. The quiet period in the *Fed's* communications is not a quiet
  period in the *market*.

*The narrow one-day pre-FOMC drift of Lucca-Moench (2015) is real and lives inside this
window — but spread across ~10 days it vanishes, and it is a different object from the
~10-day "blackout" the folklore points at.*
